title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
abstract: arXiv:2611.23068v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent evolution follows a simple loop: a proposer writes candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories) and selection accepts those that score higher. This loop has shown promise, yet practitioners face a puzzle: methods trade wins across papers, and evolution often fails to bootstrap on certain tasks. We trace this puzzle to the Resolution Hypothesis: agent evolution stalls not because methods fail to propose better artifacts, but because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify them. Across seven evolution methods and six models (over 10M LLM calls), we find support for the hypothesis at both levels where evaluation scores are used. At the candidate level (choosing artifacts), helpful candidate artifacts exist, but selection is no better than random at telling them from harmful ones, so errors accumulate across rounds. translated_title: 分辨率假说：智能体进化的关键在于识别改进
translated_abstract: 智能体进化遵循一个简单的循环：提议者撰写候选产物（如提示词、技能、记忆），选择机制则接受得分更高的那些候选产物。这一循环已展现出前景，但实践者面临一个难题：不同方法在各篇论文中互有胜负，且进化在某些任务上常常无法实现自我提升。我们将这一难题归结为分辨率假说：智能体进化停滞，并非因为方法无法提出更好的产物，而是因为带有噪声的评估无法可靠地识别出这些更好的产物。通过跨越七种进化方法和六个模型（超过1000万次LLM调用）的实验，我们发现该假说在所有使用评估得分的两个层面都得到了支持。在候选层面（选择产物）上，有益的候选产物确实存在，但选择机制在区分有益与有害产物方面的表现并不比随机更好，因此误差在多轮迭代中不断累积。在方法层面（对方法进行排名）上，典型的几个百分点的差距小于……
tldr: 智能体进化的停滞并非因为方法无法提出更好的候选产物，而是因为噪声评估无法可靠地识别出这些改进，使得选择的效果与随机无异。
en_tdlr: Agent evolution stalls not because methods fail to propose better artifacts, but because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify them, making selection no better than random.
